results.answer: All nine simple modules over the trivial extension $T=A\ltimes D(A)$ have $\Omega$-period 8, so the sum of the $\Omega$-periods is $9\cdot 8=72$.
results.method: Built the quiver of T (linear quiver plus arrows from the bimodule socle paths [1,5],[2,6],[4,7],[6,8],[7,9]), lifted to the repetitive algebra, and computed minimal projective resolutions of all 9 simples; each returned the same simple after 8 steps (4 copy-shifts).

results.answer: Every one of the 9 simple modules over the trivial extension T = A ⋉ D(A) has Ω-period 8, so the sum of the Ω-periods is 9 × 8 = 72.
results.method: Built T explicitly (quiver = A_9 line plus arrows 5→1,6→2,7→4,8→6,9→7 dual to maximal paths), described all 9 projective T-modules basis-wise, then computed minimal projective resolutions of each simple; each returned to itself after exactly 8 steps.

results.answer: All nine simple modules over the trivial extension T = A ⋉ D(A) (a symmetric algebra of dimension 60) have Ω-period exactly 8, so the sum of the Ω-periods is 9·8 = 72.
results.method: Built T explicitly: quiver = linear arrows 1→…→9 plus duals of maximal paths (5→1,6→2,7→4,8→6,9→7); wrote all 9 projectives (dims 6,7,7,8,8,8,7,5,4) and computed minimal syzygies of each simple by hand; every chain closed at Ω^8.

results.answer: There are 75 distinct Luna types for representations of Q with d=(1,3,4,1), taken over all stability conditions admitting semistables (16 with a single part containing both vertices 1 and 4, plus 59 with separate parts for vertices 1 and 4).
results.method: Enumerated decompositions d=Σm_i e_i with a common θ making each e_i stable, using Schofield's generic-subrepresentation criterion (⟨f,e-f⟩≥0 plus hom computations) to get cone conditions on θ; Kronecker parts are multiples of one primitive, counted by partitions of gcd.

results.answer: 84 distinct Luna types occur for Q with d=(1,3,4,1) over all stability conditions admitting semistables (counting a Luna type as a multiset of pairs (stable dimension vector, multiplicity)).
results.method: Listed Schur subroots of d; used sink/source subrepresentation and Schofield ext criteria to get exact stability inequalities (θ3>0, θ4<0, q>-c/b etc.); enumerated θ in the 2-dim space d^perp by cases (one summand at vertex 1, one at 4, middle summands of fixed slope), then counted multiplicity partitions: 1+16+62+5=84.

results.answer: 84 distinct Luna types. (A Luna type is a datum {e: partition} with e a θ-stable Schur root and Σ|p^e|·e = (1,3,4,1); the union over all θ admitting semistables, including θ=0, has 84 members.)
results.method: Enumerated Schur roots ≤ d via Tits form, computed generic sub-dimension vectors (Schofield) to get θ-stability inequalities, then classified all decompositions d=Σ m_i e_i admitting a common θ, decorating repeated summands by partitions.
